record.context_brief: reachability of stable matchings in the divorce digraph
record.original_question: Given a Stable Marriage instance I and an arbitrary matching M0, decide the complexity of determining whether the divorce digraph D_I contains a path from the vertex v_{M0} to some sink vertex, equivalently to a stable matching.

evidence.quote: This leads to a natural open question, namely to resolve the complexity of the following decision problem: given an sm instance I and a matching M0, is there a path in DI from vM0 to a sink vertex?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let I be an instance of the Stable Marriage problem consisting of two disjoint sets U and W of n agents (men and women), where each agent has a strict total order over the agents of the opposite set. A matching M is a set of disjoint man-woman pairs. A pair (m, w) ∉ M is called blocking for M if m prefers w to his partner in M (or is unmatched in M) and w prefers m to her partner in M (or is unmatched). A matching is stable if it admits no blocking pair.

Define the divorce digraph D_I as the directed graph whose vertex set consists of all matchings of I (including unstable and possibly non-perfect ones), and which contains an arc from M to M' whenever M' is obtained from M by "satisfying" one blocking pair (m, w) of M: that is, m and w are matched together in M', any previous partners of m and w in M become unmatched in M', and all other pairs of M are unchanged. The sinks of D_I are exactly the stable matchings of I.

For a matching M_0 of I let v_{M_0} denote the corresponding vertex of D_I. Determine the computational complexity of the following decision problem:

Input: a Stable Marriage instance I and a matching M_0 of I.
Question: does D_I contain a directed path from v_{M_0} to some sink vertex?
artifact.status_search_result: Web searches surface related work on paths to stability and improved algorithms in the divorce/better-response digraph, but no reference resolves the complexity of deciding whether some sequence of blocking-pair resolutions starting from an arbitrary matching M_0 can reach a stable matching. The problem appears to still be open.

status_evidence.title: Improved Paths to Stability for the Stable Marriage Problem
status_evidence.snippet: Recent work on paths to stability in stable marriage, addressing algorithms for reaching stable matchings via blocking-pair resolutions but not resolving the general reachability decision complexity.
status_evidence.claim: Subsequent literature on paths to stability does not appear to settle the reachability complexity question.

status_evidence.title: Paths to marriage stability
status_evidence.snippet: Roth and Vande Vate's classical result that random better-response paths reach stability with probability 1, but no characterization of which starting matchings admit such a path under adversarial choice.
status_evidence.claim: Existence-with-probability-1 results do not address the decision complexity from an arbitrary matching.
